result.topic_en: Euler shows that a spherical shell, and hence a sphere whose density depends only on distance from the centre, is attracted by the Sun or Moon as if all its matter were at the centre, and applies this to the Earth.
result.transcription:

directione $MS$ vi acceleratrice $= \frac{S}{MS^2} = \frac{S}{xx+yy}$, positâ
cùm vi gravitatis naturalis in superficie Terrae $= 1$: atque hanc ob rem ele-
mentum $Mm$ versùs $S$ nitetur vi $= \frac{S.Mm}{xx+yy}$. Resolvatur haec
vis in binas laterales, quarum alterius directio cadat in
$MP$, alterius verò sit parallela directioni $PS$; atque evi-
dens erit vires omnes $MP$ per totam peripheriam se mu-
tuò destruere, alterarum verò mediam directionem iisdem con-
junctim sumtis fore aequalem. Trahetur autem elementum
$Mm$ in directione ipsi $PS$ parallela vi $= \frac{Sx.Mm}{(xx+yy)^{\frac{3}{2}}}$, unde po-
sitâ ratione radii ad peripheriam $= 1:\pi$ tota circuli $MN$ pe-
ripheria, quae erit $= \pi y$, urgebitur seu quasi gravitabit versùs
$S$ in ipsâ directione $PS$ vi $= \frac{\pi Sxy}{(xx+yy)^{\frac{3}{2}}}$. Vis autem accele-
ratrix quâ haec peripheria circuli versùs $S$ sollicitabitur, pro-
dibit, si vis motrix inventa dividatur per massam moven-
dam, quae est $= \pi y$, eritque $= \frac{Sx}{(xx+yy)^{\frac{3}{2}}}$.
§. 20. Hoc praemisso, contemplemur superficiem sphaeri-
cam genitam conversione circuli $AMB$ circa diametrum
$AB$; sitque semidiameter $AC = BC = r$; erit ipsa superfi-
cies $= 2\pi rr$. Jam attrahatur haec superficies ad Solem Lu-
namve in $S$, existente distantiâ $SC = a$; atque ad vim to-
talem seu conatum quo integra superficies ad $S$ tendet,
inveniendum, concipiatur annulus genitus conversione ele-
menti $Mm$ circa diametrum $AB$, quae protensa per $S$
transeat. Positis igitur $SP = x$, $PM = y$, erit per §. praec.
conatus hujus annuli in directione $PS = \frac{\pi Sxy.Mm}{(xx+yy)^{\frac{3}{2}}}$. At
posito $Pp = dx$, erit $Mm = \frac{rdx}{y}$, & $xx+yy = 2ax -$
$aa + rr$, unde annuli conatus versùs $S$ erit $= \frac{\pi Srxdx}{(2ax-aa+rr)^{\frac{3}{2}}}$,
cujus integrale est $= C + \frac{\pi Sr(ax-aa+rr)}{\sqrt{(2ax-aa+rr)}}$, ex quo cona-
tus portionis superficiei sphaericae conversione arcus $AM$

FLUXUS AC REFLUXUS MARIS. 253
ortae prodibit $= \frac{\pi Srr}{aa} + \frac{\pi Sr(ax-aa+rr)}{\sqrt{(2ax-aa+rr)}}$. Quare si ponatur
$SP = SB$ seu $x = a + r$, emerget conatus totius superficiei
sphaericae $= \frac{2\pi Srr}{aa}$: hincque cùm ipsa superficies sit $=$
$2\pi rr$, erit vis acceleratrix quâ superficies sphaerica actu
versùs $S$ tendet $= \frac{S}{aa}$, ideoque tanta, quanta foret, si
tota superficies in centro $C$ esset collecta.
§. 21. Cùm igitur superficies sphaerica perinde ad So-
lem sive Lunam in $S$ sollicitetur, ac si tota in ipso centro
esset conflata, haec proprietas ad omnes superficies sphae-
ricas, ex quibus integra Sphaera composita concipi potest,
patebit, dummodò singulae hae superficies ex materiâ homo-
geneâ constent, sive quod eodem redit, ipsa Sphaera in iis-
dem à centro distantiis sit aequè densa. Hanc ob rem ejus-
modi Sphaera quoque perinde ad $S$ in directione $PS$ ur-
gebitur, ac si tota ipsius materia in centro $C$ esset concen-
trata; haecque proprietas non solùm in ejusmodi Sphaeras
competit, quae totae ex materiâ uniformi sunt confectae,
sed etiam ut jam indicavimus, in tales, quae ex materiâ
constant difformi, dummodo in aequalibus à centro distantiis,
materia circumquaque sit homogenea seu saltem ejusdem
densitatis. Cùm igitur Terram sibi repraesentare liceat tan-
quam Sphaeram, si non ex uniformi materiâ conflatam, tamen
sine ullo errore ita comparatam, ut in aequalibus circa
centrum intervallis materiam aequè densam includat, Terra
quoque universa tàm à Sole quàm à Lunâ aequè sollici-
tabitur, ac si omnis ejus materia in centro esset collecta.
Quanquam enim nunc quidem accuratissimis ab Illustrissi-
mâ Academiâ Regiâ institutis passim mensuris satis est de-
monstratum, Terrae figuram ad polos esse compressam,
tamen tantilla à perfectâ Sphaerâ aberratio, in aliis quidem
negotiis maximi momenti, in hoc instituto tutò negligi
potest. Parique ratione, etiamsi Terra in aequalibus à cen-
tro distantiis non sit aequè densa, tamen differentia certè
non est tanta, ut error sensibilis inde sit metuendus.

items.english: The accelerative force with which the spherical surface actually tends toward S will be S/aa, and hence as great as it would be if the whole surface were collected at the centre C.

items.quote:
Hanc ob rem ejus-
modi Sphaera quoque perinde ad $S$ in directione $PS$ ur-
gebitur, ac si tota ipsius materia in centro $C$ esset concen-
trata
items.english: For this reason such a sphere will also be urged toward S in the direction PS just as if all its matter were concentrated at the centre C.

items.quote:
tamen tantilla à perfectâ Sphaerâ aberratio, in aliis quidem
negotiis maximi momenti, in hoc instituto tutò negligi
potest.
items.english: Yet so small a deviation from a perfect sphere, though of the greatest importance in other matters, can safely be neglected in this undertaking.

items.quote:
tamen differentia certè
non est tanta, ut error sensibilis inde sit metuendus.
items.english: Yet the difference is certainly not so great that a sensible error need be feared from it.
